name: Babcock Hall
use: All-single residence for students 21 and older (graduate, international and undergraduate)
style: Late-1960s modern slab: exposed-aggregate precast panels between brick piers (from photo)

facts.text: Dedicated March 16, 1968 and named for philosophy professor Donald C. Babcock.

Designed by Carter & Woodruff and built by Davison Construction; it was the first UNH residence designed specifically for graduate students and was first called Babcock House as a combined residence and graduate studies center. First residents moved in January 29, 1968.
Today it houses a community aged 21 and older (international, graduate and undergraduate) in single rooms, each with a mini fridge.

Features listed: elevator, inside bike storage, kitchen, laundry, lounges including one with a fireplace, sand volleyball court; floor plans for five floors; gender-inclusive bathrooms on the 2nd floor.

photos.caption: Babcock Hall: precast-panel wings and brick stair towers

verdict: 1968 precast-panel slab for over-21 singles; utilitarian outside, no A/C, no renovation on record.
notes: Photo (Commons, July 2005, described by the uploader as Babcock Hall): a tall slab of grey exposed-aggregate precast panels framed by full-height red-brick piers, with a glazed stair/lounge stack; utilitarian and dated, competent proportions, no ornament. No interior photos seen. No AC listed by Housing. No renovation documented. No student reviews found (old row cited MyDorm with 0 reviews; not rechecked).
judgeNotes: Photo shows a grey exposed-aggregate slab between brick piers: dated and blunt. No interior evidence.
